description: The administrator's only screen. They create the staff accounts the workflow needs, change a person's role, activate or suspend an account, and grant or revoke individual capabilities. An admin never reads or touches a request — this is the one thing they can do, and everything about the app's authorization is decided here.

trpc_procedures.name: listAllUsers
guards: the select list never includes a password or a session token
trpc_procedures.description: Paginated account list. Search matches name or email, case-insensitive. Newest first.

trpc_procedures.name: createStaffAccount
guards: the role must be one of the four staff roles — USER and ADMIN are rejected
confirmPassword is stripped by a schema .transform before the handler
trpc_procedures.description: Creates the user and its better-auth credential Account with a hashed password, sets emailVerified true and status active, then seeds the role's default permissions. profileComplete stays false so the new staff member is sent to /profile to add a signature before they can approve anything.

trpc_procedures.name: updateUserRole
guards: ADMIN is not an assignable target role
trpc_procedures.description: Updates the role, then calls resetAndSeedPermissions so the person holds exactly the new role's defaults and nothing carried over.

trpc_procedures.name: updateUserStatus
trpc_procedures.description: The account switch. protectedProcedure reads status on every call, so a non-active account can hold a session and still do nothing.

trpc_procedures.name: resetToRoleDefaults
trpc_procedures.description: Reads the user's current role and reapplies its defaults, wiping anything hand-set.

functional: Staff accounts are created here and nowhere else. Requestors self-register (spec 002); admins come from the seed.
A created staff account is active and email-verified — there is no mail provider, so an unverified staff account would be stuck at /verify-email forever.
profileComplete starts false, so a new staff member is sent to /profile to add the signature their approvals require.
The password is set by the admin and handed over out of band. There is no invitation email and no forced rotation.
Changing a role RESETS permissions to the new role's defaults. Nothing carries over.
Permission switches save on toggle, with no Save button.
ACTION_LABELS supplies the label and description for each switch, so the seven capabilities are described in one place (spec 001).
The table shows whether each account has completed its profile, because an approver without a signature is a queue that will stall.
Role and status are chips, so an admin scanning forty accounts can see the shape of the org.
authorization: Route gate: the /admin layout route uses assertAuthenticatedRoleFn with ['ADMIN'].
Server gate: every procedure here is an adminProcedure. Not one of them falls back to an inline role check.
An admin may not change their own role or their own status — the self-check is on both procedures, and it is what stops the last administrator locking themselves out.
createStaffAccount rejects USER and ADMIN as target roles. Self-registration is the only path to USER, and ADMIN accounts are seeded deliberately.
The user list never selects a password hash, a session token or anything from the account table.
An ADMIN has no read access to requests at all — request.getById excludes them by design (spec 006). Nothing on this page changes that.
ux: Every consequence is stated where the action is taken: the role modal says permissions will be reset, the status modal says what each state means for the person, the create modal says the account starts active and needs a signature.
Suspension is confirmed; activation is not. Confirmation belongs on the destructive direction only.
Permission toggles show a pending state per switch and revert visibly if the call fails — a switch that silently springs back is how an admin believes they revoked something they did not.
The empty state offers New Staff Account.
The self-row's role and status actions are disabled with a tooltip explaining why, rather than failing on press.

edge_cases: The self-guard is the only thing standing between an admin and a locked system. It belongs on both role and status, and it must compare against ctx.user.id, never against a field in the payload.
createStaffAccount writes two rows — the user and the better-auth credential Account. If the second fails, the user exists and cannot sign in; wrap both in one transaction.
Permissions are seeded after creation. A failure there leaves a staff member who can sign in and do nothing; make the failure loud rather than swallowed.

There is only ever one ADMIN by default and the endpoint refuses to create more. If the seeded admin's password is lost there is no recovery path — say so in the runbook, or add a second seeded admin deliberately.

Revoking a permission does not remove a request from that person's queue; the row stays and the action fails. The review pages must therefore disable their controls on the permission too, not only on the stage.
Password hashing must use better-auth's own hashPassword, or the created account cannot sign in and the failure looks like a wrong password.
User.status defaults to inactive after spec 001, so createStaffAccount setting 'active' explicitly is load-bearing, not decoration.
out_of_scope: Password reset for another user — the admin sets a temporary password at creation; there is no admin-triggered reset. Users use /forgot-password.
Deleting an account — status is the switch. A deletion would orphan requests, audit logs and signatures.
Creating a second ADMIN — deliberately not possible through the UI.
Bulk import or CSV — a handful of staff accounts is the whole scale.
An admin view of requests — an admin manages accounts and reads no request. This is enforced in spec 006 and is not softened here.
Audit logging of admin actions — the AuditLog is per request; admin actions are logged only to the application logger.
